questions.title: Orbits of planets, moons and comets
questions.stimulus: The diagram shows the orbits of a planet, its moon, and a comet in our Solar System (which lies inside the Milky Way galaxy).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the force that causes the planet to orbit the Sun and the moon to orbit the planet.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe two differences between the orbit of the planet and the orbit of the comet.

points.text: The planet's orbit is nearly circular, whereas the comet's orbit is highly elliptical
The Sun is near the centre of the planet's orbit, whereas the Sun is off-centre (near one end) of the comet's orbit
The planet moves at a nearly constant speed, whereas the comet's speed changes greatly during its orbit

accept: planet stays roughly the same distance from the Sun while comet's distance varies greatly

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how the speed of the comet at position X compares with its speed at position Y.

points.text: The comet travels faster at X (and slower at Y)
At X the comet is closer to the Sun, so the gravitational force pulling it is stronger (or GPE has transferred to kinetic energy)

reject: gravity is the same at X and Y

questions.title: Orbital speed of a low-Earth satellite
questions.stimulus: An Earth-observation satellite travels in a circular orbit at an altitude of 600 km above Earth's surface. Earth's radius is 6400 km, and the satellite completes one full orbit every 98 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the orbital radius r of the satellite in metres.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the orbital speed of the satellite in m/s. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.

points.text: Formula & time conversion: v = 2 × π × rT and T = 98 × 60 = 5880 s

accept: ECF from part (a) if r was substituted correctly into 2πr / T
reject: 448 800 m/s (using T = 98 min without converting to seconds)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Even though the satellite moves at a constant speed, its velocity is constantly changing. State why.

points.text: Its direction of motion is constantly changing (and velocity is a vector quantity)

questions.title: Evolution of Sun-like and massive stars
questions.stimulus: The flowchart summarises the life cycles of stars of similar mass to the Sun and stars with a much larger mass than the Sun.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the missing stage marked ? in the life cycle of a star of similar mass to the Sun.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a main sequence star remains stable in size for billions of years.

points.text: Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in the core releases energy, creating outward radiation / gas pressure
Balances the inward pull of gravitational force (forces are in equilibrium)

accept: inward gravity equals outward thermal/radiation pressure
reject: no forces act on the star

parts.label: c
parts.text: For a star much more massive than the Sun, describe what happens at the supernova stage.

points.text: The red supergiant undergoes a massive explosion (throwing outer layers into space and leaving a dense core — a neutron star or black hole)

questions.title: Star colour, surface temperature and gravity
questions.stimulus: Astronomers measure the surface temperature and colour of four main-sequence stars: P, Q, R and S.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the relationship between a star's surface temperature and its colour.

points.text: The hotter the star, the closer its colour is to blue-white / blue (and the cooler the star, the closer to red)

parts.label: b
parts.text: A newly discovered star has a surface temperature of 10 200 K. Use the chart to predict its colour.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The gravitational field strength g is 25 N/kg on Jupiter compared with 10 N/kg on Earth. State the main reason why g is greater on Jupiter.

points.text: Jupiter has a much larger mass than Earth

reject: Jupiter is bigger (volume/size alone without mentioning mass)
Jupiter is further from the Sun
